items.title: Applied Materials slips as investors seek faster growth after stellar run
items.summary: Applied Materials shares fell about 5% in premarket trading on Friday, as the ‌chip equipment maker's upbeat outlook failed to ‌soothe investors worried about the threat from intensifying competition.  The muted reaction ​illustrates the high bar chip stocks have to clear and suggests that investors have little tolerance for any hint that a company may be falling behind peers.  After a ‌sharp rally that ⁠has more than doubled Applied's shares this year, investors want clearer signals that the ⁠company's growth is outpacing rivals in the wafer-fab-equipment market.

items.title: Why Lam Research (LRCX) Is Up 10.2% After $3 Billion Global R&D Lab Expansion Plan
items.summary: In August 2026, Lam Research announced plans to invest more than US$3.00 billion over five years to expand its global R&D lab network, aiming to lift experiment capacity by over 50% and compress product development cycles for semiconductor customers across the US, Asia, and Europe. An interesting angle is how this integrated 24/7 lab system, which already supports over one million experiments annually, is being scaled to accelerate AI-era chip innovation through faster, closer collaboration...

items.title: Chip equipment maker Lam Research to invest more than $3 billion to expand R&D labs
items.summary: Lam Research said on Thursday it intends to invest more than $3 billion in ‌the next five years to expand its ‌global research and development lab network, as it seeks to increase ​experiment capacity and speed up product development.  The U.S. chip equipment maker said the multi-site expansion is expected to increase its experiment capacity by over 50%.  • Lam Research is making the investment with the intention of staying ahead of customers' ​needs as ​the pace of innovation ​requires chips with new ‌architectures, different materials and complex features engineered with nanoscale precision, CEO Tim Archer said.

items.title: Applied Materials forecasts revenue above estimates, shares fall on high expectations
items.summary: Applied Materials forecast fourth-quarter revenue above Wall Street expectations on Thursday, betting that unabated demand for advanced AI ‌chips will continue to fuel robust spending on its semiconductor manufacturing equipment.  Even ‌so, its shares dropped more than 5% in extended trading as lofty investor expectations overshadowed the results.  Expectations are elevated as the chip equipment maker reports after peers Lam Research and KLA posted solid quarterly performances and forecast revenue growth, Stifel's Brian Chin said.

items.title: KLA Drops 9% in a Month: Should You Buy the Stock on the Dip?
items.summary: KLAC's 9.3% monthly drop highlights near-term margin and supply risks, even as AI demand, HBM and advanced packaging support its long-term growth outlook.
